blogs.title: Why Bytes Might Soon Replace Tokens: Introducing the Byte Latent Transformer
blogs.description: An overview of the new BLT architecture that abandons fixed vocabularies for raw bytes, explaining how dynamic patching works and why it can match or beat traditional token‑based LLMs at scale.

blogs.title: Dynamic Patching 101: How Entropy‑Based Byte Groups Make LLMs Faster
blogs.description: A deep dive into the three patching strategies (static stride, whitespace, entropy‑based), focusing on the entropy‑patching method, how next‑byte uncertainty drives patch boundaries, and the resulting inference‑flop savings.

blogs.title: Scaling Laws for Byte‑Level Models: From 400 M to 8 B Parameters
blogs.description: Translates the FLOP‑controlled scaling experiments into plain language, showing how BLT keeps pace with Llama 3, how larger patches unlock new scaling dimensions, and what this means for future model growth.

blogs.title: Robustness by Design: How Byte‑Level LLMs Handle Noisy Text and Low‑Resource Languages
blogs.description: Summarizes the robustness tests (noisy inputs, phonology, CUTE benchmark, low‑resource MT), highlighting why direct byte modeling improves character‑level understanding and multilingual equity.

blogs.title: From Tokenizer to Byte Model: Turning a Pre‑trained Llama 3 into a BLT
blogs.description: Explains the “byte‑ifying” workflow that initializes BLT’s global transformer from a token‑based model, the benefits of faster convergence, and early results showing performance gains with far fewer training FLOPs.
